title: Missing complexity metrics are displayed as measured zeros
reasoning: When mass.cc or cc_concentration is absent, assigning the scalar default 0 creates a zero measurement for every checkpoint. The histogram then displays a populated distribution at zero, suggesting measured low complexity instead of unavailable analysis. Creating these columns also defeats build_histogram's existing missing-column guard.
reproduction: Provide a nonempty checkpoint dataframe without mass.cc and cc_concentration. Both complexity histograms receive one zero per checkpoint.
recommendation: Pass the original metric columns to build_histogram, or preserve missing values and explicitly display unavailable data. Do not synthesize zero measurements.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were included in the supplied feature context; missing-metric coverage cannot be verified.
suggestedRegressionTest: Exercise quality rendering with present, partially missing, and absent metric data. Assert that only actual measurements contribute to histogram counts and absent metrics produce an empty or unavailable state.
minimumFixScope: Metric preparation in update_quality and focused quality-rendering coverage.
